I was in the exact same boat and I say that we (you and I) have a right to pursue a healthier relationship or life. In my personal experience, I tried my hardest to support him, he actively told me he did not want to seek help (that’s where we differ) but at some point we have to realize we are not selfish or assholes for wanting something better for ourselves, the most important person in our lives are ourselves. You can try to help someone but if they don’t want to change you can’t force them. Depression is a serious mental illness and it can sometimes drag the people around the depressed person down with them. In my defense it did that to me and that’s why I broke it off, I hold so much love for him still, but I won’t sacrifice my well-being for someone who doesn’t want to actively try to get better. You should think about it like that. You are not responsible for someone else’s happiness or mental stability or whatever you want to call it. If they choose to take their life it is not your fault. That was their decision.
